He shares his prediction from three years ago about the number of automatable jobs.

He emphasizes the significant percentage of the labor market that could be automated in the next 10-20 years.
He talks about the reactions to his initial predictions about automation.
He presents reports from Oxford Martin School and other research organizations confirming his predictions.
He reiterates that he is not an economist but his prediction about automation is now supported by established institutions.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: So a few months ago I was contacted by one of my favorite YouTubers, CGP Grey, and he asked me about the video that I've made about robots stealing jobs and what to do about it.
And I was really happy that I was getting in touch with him because he makes really cool, amazing educational videos.
If you don't know his channel, you should watch it, link in the video description.
You should watch all of his videos. But this one in particular, I thought, wow, this is amazing if he's going to make a video on automation.
I really have to give him some references and maybe he will use that.
And then months and months go by, nothing happens. I was like, yeah, that's one of his failed projects.
And then just now I saw a 15 minute video about exactly automation and how robots are stealing jobs and what to do about it.
I was really, really happy with the way he handled the video.
He presented very clear, compelling evidence that's in my book and in the conferences and also the work that others have done.
It's funny that I found a specific reference that was exactly taken from my book.
The prediction that I've made about three years ago on the number of jobs that could be automatable.
I've done a back of the envelope calculation by looking at the 50 most popular jobs in the economy.
And what I discovered is before you can pinpoint a new kind of job, so a job that was created within the last 50 years,
you have to go to something like number 33, which is computer programmers. You have to be a developer.
And every other job is a kind of job that was created maybe a hundred years ago or so.
And that represented almost half of the entire labor market.
So I predicted that within 10 to 20 years, half of all the jobs will be automated.
And the very few new jobs will be created.
So you take away 50% and maybe you create something like a 5%.
And that sounded like a now glanish claim, something that wasn't possible.
Economists, most of them didn't listen and didn't say anything.
But the few who did, they said, you're not an economist, shut up. So you need not have anything.
And then what happens?
A couple of years later, the Oxford Martis School comes out with a report saying 45% of all jobs will be automated within 20 years.
And then another report in Europe, Italy has 58% of jobs or something like that will be automated within 20 years.
Germany is 52% remaining. So around 50% of jobs will be automated 10 to 20 years from now.
And this is what most of the greatest economists and economic institutions in the world are saying right now.
And that's three to four years after I've made my prediction.
And of course, I'm not an economist. I'm not an established institution or a professor with 20 years experience that MIT or Harvard or Oxford.
But nevertheless, I know a little bit about technology and about robots and about automation and about artificial intelligence.
And I put two and two together.
And these are the things that I came up with that I was really happy that CGB Gray not only took the time to make this really, really good compelling video that presents in a very clear way.
What I've presented in my keynote speeches and in my presentations and in my book.
And he does so in a very concise, understandable way that is digestible to the public.
So I really encourage you to check out and was particularly happy that he used exactly my example.
It's straight out of my book. Good job there.
I was also eager to see if it was going to present some solutions. So what to do about it part.
And unfortunately, there was none of it, but you know, the video was already 15 minutes long.
So I understand it given time constraints. It would be impossible to actually present that as well.
But if you are interested, the good news is my book robots will steal your job.
But that's okay. Is available for free on my website.
I've been publishing every other week a new chapter right now. I'm three quarters towards the end of the book.
And I'm going to publish a new chapter right now as I publish this video until I finish all the chapters and they're all free.
And of course, if you want, you can support my work and you can get your copy on Amazon and your Kindle or whatever.
And of course, every copy is DRM free and it's released under Creative Commons license.
All right. Thank you for listening and I'll see you next time.
Ciao.
